In src/sqllens/_bounded_json.py visit(): str is length-checked against remaining_bytes (line 46) before json.dumps (line 66), so the input is bounded to remaining_bytes chars. The ensure_ascii expansion (up to 6x per char, 12x for non-BMP) only affects the output, which charge() then checks against the budget. int is checked via bit_length > remaining_bytes*4 (61), and a huge-int str conversion error is caught (67). float, bool and None are fixed-size. Other types, including str and int subclasses, are rejected at line 63 by exact type check. dict and list sizes are checked against remaining_nodes (49), depth is capped (37), and exceptions abort traversal. Hostile input tried: a long non-ASCII string. Its dumps input is at most remaining_bytes chars, so it is bounded, then rejected by charge if the escaped form overflows. No unbounded input reaches json.dumps.

src/sqllens/_bounded_json.py:51 charges 2 + max(0,n-1) per container (brackets + commas; empty =2). Line 56 charges 1 per colon; keys are charged via json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True) at line 66 (quotes and \u escapes included). Scalars use json.dumps with default separators, identical to compact encoding for scalars. Total equals len(json.dumps(tree, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True)) for accepted types (exact dict/list/str/int/float/bool/None; NaN rejected). Non-ASCII string and nested object traced: each char is charged as its escape length. Depth: visit(value,0); nodes decrement for every visit including keys (line 57, key=True). Truncated strings are counted post-truncation, which matches the returned copy. Line 46 is only a lower-bound early check. Trace of the hostile input (a non-ASCII or nested object) found no mismatch.

In _bounded_json.py:39-64, only exact-type str, int, float, bool and None reach json.dumps at line 66. Containers return earlier, and any other type raises JsonBoundsError at line 64. For these scalars, json.dumps with allow_nan=False raises ValueError on NaN or Infinity, which is the documented behavior. A huge int can raise ValueError through the int-to-str digit limit, which is also a ValueError. A str with lone surrogates encodes fine with ensure_ascii=True. There is no recursion for scalars. The only exceptions possible are therefore TypeError or ValueError, both caught at line 67.

_bounded_json.py:60-62 rejects when bit_length() > 4*remaining_bytes. Such an int is >= 2^(4R), so it has >= floor(1.204R)+1 decimal digits, which exceeds R for every R>=0 (R=0 also overflows, since '0' needs 1 byte). Negative signs only add bytes. So the check never rejects an int that would have fit; it is sound as a conservative early reject. It is not sufficient: ints with up to about 1.2R digits can pass, but line 66 then charges the real length (charge, lines 28-32) and raises on overflow. json.dumps cost on passing ints is bounded by about 4R bits, and the interpreter's int-to-str digit limit raises ValueError, which line 67 catches. bool is excluded because type(item) is int exactly.
